Retrieve World Bank data for the indicator “Gross savings (% of GDP)” (code NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS) for all economies for each year 2001–2010, handle pagination, and exclude aggregates. Filter to identify economies where every single year’s value is strictly greater than 35.0% and there are no missing values. 2. From the filtered set, compile the full year-by-year values for each candidate economy, document any borderline or excluded cases (e.g., a 35.0% year or missing data), and note sovereignty/territory status and any uncertainties. 3. After reviewing the results, map names to the most common English country names, separate lists for sovereign-only vs including territories if applicable, sort alphabetically, and present a comprehensive report of all plausible candidates, supporting evidence, and identified uncertainties. Then provide the final comma-separated list(s) per the user’s request. What we know: - The target series is World Bank NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS, “Gross savings (% of GDP).” - The period must include every year 2001–2010. - Threshold is strictly >35.0% for each year. - Any missing value disqualifies an economy. - Aggregates (regions, income groups) must be excluded. What’s missing: - The actual list of qualifying economies and their yearly values. - Clarification on borderline cases and classification of territories. Tool choice: - I will use the web-capable agent to query the World Bank API, handle pagination, exclude aggregates via country metadata, and produce a processed summary with the filtered list and the evidence table. This directly advances Step 1. [msg_b65d07b8] Final report: Economies with Gross savings (% of GDP) strictly > 35.0 in every year 2001–2010, using World Bank API (indicator NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS) Task overview - Objective: Identify all non-aggregate economies whose Gross savings (% of GDP) exceeded 35.0 in each year from 2001 through 2010 (inclusive), with no missing values. Values equal to 35.0 do not qualify. Use exactly the values returned by the World Bank API and exclude aggregates/groupings. Data retrieval and processing methodology - Indicator data endpoint: - https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS?date=2001:2010&per_page=20000&format=json - Pagination handling: Queried page 1; the API reported pages=1 for this request, so all records were retrieved in a single request. - Economy metadata endpoint (to exclude aggregates/groupings): - https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/{id}?format=json - Exclusion rule: Drop entries where country.region.value == “Aggregates” or country.region.id == “NA”. - Value handling and filtering: - Used the values exactly as provided by the API, preserving the reported decimals (typically one decimal). - For each non-aggregate economy, verified that for every year 2001–2010: - The value is present (not null/missing). - The value is strictly greater than 35.0 (i.e., >35.0). Any instance of exactly 35.0 disqualifies the economy. - Near-miss definition: - An economy with 9 years strictly >35.0 and exactly one year failing due to being 35.0 or missing (with no <35.0 years) is documented as a near-miss. - Documentation counts: - Indicator endpoint pages requested: 1. - Country metadata endpoint requests: 266 unique economy codes encountered (non-aggregates included in evaluation; aggregates excluded from final results). Working history and tool-execution trajectory (concise) - Created an isolated environment and wrote Python code to: 1) Retrieve NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS data for 2001–2010 with pagination and record raw values. 2) Retrieve economy-level metadata for each code and exclude aggregates/groupings. 3) Evaluate each non-aggregate economy across all ten years with strict >35.0 and no missing values. 4) Produce structured outputs: qualifying list with per-year values; near-miss notes; and economies disqualified due to missing years. - Initial pass inadvertently displayed some aggregates; logic was corrected using metadata (region.id/value) to exclude them. - Correct pass identified the three qualifying economies listed below and flagged Morocco explicitly as a near-miss (exact 35.0 in 2010). A subsequent variant output erroneously listed Morocco as qualifying; the corrected, specification-compliant result is used below. Final results A. Comprehensive summary and evidence Objective and indicator - Goal: Identify all countries with World Bank “Gross savings (% of GDP)” strictly greater than 35.0 for every year from 2001 through 2010, inclusive, with no missing values. - Indicator: NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS (Gross savings, % of GDP). - Criteria: Each of the 10 years must have a reported value and each must be >35.0 (values exactly 35.0 do not qualify). Aggregates/groupings excluded. Data retrieval summary - Pulled the indicator values for all economies for 2001–2010 from the World Bank API and excluded aggregates using country metadata (region.value == “Aggregates” or region.id == “NA”). - Verified coverage and strict threshold compliance year-by-year for each non-aggregate economy. Under an alternative interpretation of “≥35.0,” Morocco would qualify. - Macao (territory/SAR) Evidence: Data missing in 2001; other years present and high. Why excluded: Any missing year in 2001–2010 disqualifies. Even under “≥35.0,” missing coverage still disqualifies. Other notes and uncertainties - Some economies (including several resource-rich states) lack complete coverage for the entire 2001–2010 period in this indicator, which automatically disqualifies them. Examples include Qatar and United Arab Emirates (missing multiple years). - Many economies had at least one year below 35.0, which disqualifies them under the strict “>35.0” rule (not exhaustively listed here, but this is the majority of non-aggregate entries). - Names in the final list use common English country names (e.g., “Brunei” rather than “Brunei Darussalam,” “China,” “Singapore”). All three are sovereign countries; no territory/SAR naming adjustments are needed. - Rounding: World Bank values are used exactly as reported. A value of 35.0 is treated as not meeting “over 35%.” Primary answer (strictly >35.0 for every year, 2001–2010; alphabetical) Brunei, China, Singapore Alternative interpretation note (if “≥35.0” were accepted, alphabetical) Brunei, China, Morocco, Singapore
